title: Congruous merit of penitential works: private opinion, not common Rome
source_text: LVII. Quod autem dicunt nonnulli Theologi Pontificii, bona quaedam opera mereri de congruo remissionem peccatorum, & donum justitiae, peculiaris est eorum sententia, ut jam indicavimus, non vero doctrina communis Ecclesiae Romanae. Neque tamen per hoc significare volunt, justitiae infusionem, & peccati remissionem operibus poenitentiae ex justitia deberi, & non esse donum Dei gratuitum, sed hoc tantum, decere bonitatem divinam, eique congruum & conveniens esse, ut illis qui vere ad Deum convertuntur, & edunt fructus poenitentia dignos, peccata remittantur, & habitualis justitia donetur: quod Theologi Reformati non negant; licet in hoc negotio, merito vocem meriti repudiant, quia non est in Scripturae usu, & sonat aliquid superbum.
pass_a_gloss: But what some Pontifical theologians say—that certain good works merit de congruo the remission of sins and the gift of righteousness—is their peculiar opinion, as we have already indicated, not the common doctrine of the Roman Church. Nor yet by this do they mean to signify that the infusion of righteousness and the remission of sin are owed from justice to works of repentance and are not a free gift of God, but only this: that it befits divine goodness, and is fitting and suitable to it, that to those who truly convert to God and bring forth fruits worthy of repentance, sins be remitted and habitual righteousness be given: which the Reformed theologians do not deny; although in this business they rightly repudiate the word merit, because it is not in Scripture's usage and sounds something proud.
pass_b_english: Congruous merit of penitential works is a private Pontifical opinion, not common Roman doctrine.
Even they mean fitting divine goodness—not a justice-debt; Reformed grant the fittingness, reject the word 'merit'.

choices.term: non vero doctrina communis Ecclesiae Romanae
choices.english: not indeed the common doctrine of the Roman Church
choices.why: Le Blanc separates private from common teaching.
